title: Fix firstmate study claims until the source check passes
summary: Add t5 to the places-held counter's changed_by in the firstmate-work-handling study, backed by a claim citing bin/fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh:845-851. Then run the model-backed source check, correct each further claim it reports with a citation to the pinned source, and repeat until it reports no findings. The audience is the study-page reader and the study rules/source check.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria require the source check to report no findings, not just that edits were made.
Every corrected claim cites the pinned source file and lines.
Acceptance checks the check's result, not file existence.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/pin.rs (source_check_brief, check_study_text, which is a model-backed read of the study text against the pinned tree) and xtask/src/main.rs (no study-check subcommand exists; xtask only has setup, ci, site, etc.), and crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs (check_study rules). The 'source check' is therefore run by Athena's study capability, not by an xtask command.
The producer cannot necessarily run the model-backed check itself; it fixes claims by reading the pinned source and relies on the recorded check result for verification.
Environment: the pinned firstmate source is reached via pin.json (read-only); no push or CI workflow changes.
No governance files (athena.toml, defaults.toml, workflows) need to change.

acceptance_criteria.text: studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json: the places-held counter's changed_by includes t5, and claims.json has a claim for it citing bin/fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh lines 845-851 (task record removed before the backlog close), referenced from the counter's claims list.

Run cargo test; the study rules checks over studies/firstmate-work-handling (athena-cap-study rules) pass, so ids, citations and cross-references among model.json, claims.json, rationales.json and findings.json are consistent.
Run cargo clippy and cargo fmt --check; both pass.

Every further claim the source check reported is corrected in the diff with a citation to the pinned source (pin.json sha), not deleted or weakened; the recorded source check output on the final tree shows no findings for the study page.

out_of_scope: Changing the source check or study rules code
Re-pinning the study to a different commit
departures: The check reports one wrong claim per run, so an unknown number of fix-and-recheck iterations makes cost and time higher than reference.
